dw_a_dosimeter_for_time.description: I've built a second dosimeter, one that measures time instead of fallout. There's a pendulum inside it, and in some parts of the east the pendulum stops in the middle of a swing. I need readings from three of those stopped places, and I need to know whether they're growing. Go east over the ford, down the gorge and up the ramp on the far side. If the pendulum stops while you're holding it, step back until it starts again.
dw_a_dosimeter_for_time.accept_text: Wind it before you set out, and wind it again at each place. It runs down faster out there.

dw_a_name_worn_away.description: My family buried their dead at Morgan's Plot for two hundred years, and my son lies in the crypt on the north side. When the tear opened, time ran fast over the Plot for a moment, and his name was worn off the stone. I can't read it any more. I'd like someone to try, in case it's only my eyes. It's the small crypt on the north side, with the angel beside it.
dw_a_name_worn_away.accept_text: Go in daylight if you can. The letters are shallow, and you'll need the light across them.

dw_a_sample_of_her_own.description: I took one of Morwen's vials out of the sealed store, and I don't know what to do with it. I could send it to the Royal Apothecary Society, or I could throw it in the pyre. Before I decide, I want Morwen to know that someone has found out. I want it to be you who hands it to her, not me. If she lies to you, I'll know what to do with it, and if she doesn't, I'll have to think.
dw_a_sample_of_her_own.accept_text: Give it to her and see what she says.

dw_again_and_again.description: The tear kept a copy of my Edwin's last moment, and it plays it over and over at Coachman's Bend. The coach, the ice, the drop, a thousand times. The Wagon Driver is what's left of him. If he's stopped outside that moment, the next crash won't come. Catch him before he reaches the edge, and be gentle with him if you can.
dw_again_and_again.accept_text: Speak to him before you raise a hand. He might hear you, this once.

dw_archivist_nine.description: Ariden's pages were written by Karazhan's librarian at nine different ages, and I've worked out where he went. The rim's north chamber is shelved with black glass, every moment the tear has kept is filed on it, and the librarian is still writing. We call him Archivist Nine. I want his first page, the one about the night the tear opened. The Stacks are the north chamber, round the rim past the Brood.
dw_archivist_nine.accept_text: Bring his first page back flat. I'll want to read it in the order he wrote it.

dw_broodmother_vexis.description: The Silk Mother wasn't the first widow queen in Deadwind. Broodmother Vexis went down into the tear a month before the camp was built, and the liquidators found her in the rim's west chamber, fused with her own clutch. I want her heart, sealed. I've promised Dr. Seitkali I'll burn the rest, and she's going to watch me do it. Vexis is in the Brood, the west chamber, round the rim from the crater floor.
dw_broodmother_vexis.accept_text: Wear gloves when you cut it out. Her clutch went into her, and I don't know what went into the clutch.

dw_burn_the_brood.description: The Silk Mother has grown into her own cocoon at the bottom of the Widows' Nest, and every egg she lays carries the Seep out into the pass. I want her killed and the brood burned, all of it. Morwen Ashgrave wants the last egg alive for her studies, and only one of us can have it. The brood is at the top of the Throat, past the retreat holes. Morwen will argue, and I don't care.
dw_burn_the_brood.accept_text: The brood's at the top of the Throat. Kill the Silk Mother and burn everything she's sitting on.

dw_deep_samples.description: I want a sample from the very bottom of the Bubbler Pools, before the Wound's Heart dies and the seep changes. I've decided which report I'm sending, and I need the samples to prove it. The Bubbler Oozes live round the pools in the Reactor Hall's flooded basement. Seal each flask before you lift it out. Don't spill a drop on your boots.
dw_deep_samples.accept_text: Lower the flasks slowly. If you stir the bottom, the sample's worthless.

dw_downwind.description: When the wind comes off the middle of the pass, the Fused Bats ride it west and roost in the tunnel. They carry the fallout on their wings, and I've watched them do it every evening for a week. They hunt over the Sickwater at dusk. I want them dead before they carry any more of it toward people. You'll want a scarf over your mouth.
dw_downwind.accept_text: Go just before dusk. You'll catch them leaving the tunnel, before they spread out.

dw_flicker_hounds.description: I watch the middle of the pass for the Dark Lady, and the Flicker Hounds hunt my scouts across the Ashen Rise. They're never quite where you see them, because a moment of them is always a little ahead. My first scout lost an arm learning that. They run the open ground between the gorge and the rupture. Aim where they're about to be.
dw_flicker_hounds.accept_text: If you can only see one, there are two. Keep that in mind.

dw_glow_in_the_rock.description: The fallout is getting into the rock of the tunnel, and things are growing out of it where it pools. I call them slagcrawlers, and every week there are more of them between my fence and the fen. When we opened this crossing the rock was clean all the way down, and that was only a year ago. The Tunnel Slagcrawlers are in the tunnel south of the fence, mostly where the walls glow. Clear them out before they reach the Stranglethorn end.
dw_glow_in_the_rock.accept_text: Don't touch the walls where they glow, and wash your hands at the barrel when you're back anyway.

dw_gristlemaw.description: Grull says some of Grosh'gok's ogres walked into the crater the night the tear opened, and the wound made them into one body. The liquidators call it Gristlemaw, and it holds the crater floor at the bottom of the Exclusion Zone's rim. Grull asked me to send someone, and I'm sending you. The Exclusion Zone's door is in the glow crater at the foot of the wheel, and Gristlemaw's on the crater floor, right where you climb down. Take friends with you.
dw_gristlemaw.accept_text: Keep clear of the heap it stands in. It'll try to pull you in.

dw_hannas_potatoes.description: I live on my own in a lean-to in the dead forest, west of Deadman's Crossing, and I grow potatoes in the poisoned ground. The liquidators have asked me a dozen times to move into the Watch, and a dozen times I've said no. I've lived in poisoned ground before. Now the Pustule Boars have found my garden, and they come out of the trees at dawn. Chase them off for good, because I'm too old to sit up all night with a stick.
dw_hannas_potatoes.accept_text: Mind the rows when you chase them. I've only just got the second crop in.

dw_its_a_mouth.description: I've almost finished my sentence now. Go south-east, to the edge of the glow crater at the foot of the wheel. Look down into it, and you'll see what I saw. I went in alone, and I'd like you to do better than I did. Don't go in alone yourself.
dw_its_a_mouth.accept_text: Look, and then come back to me without going any closer.

dw_let_him_go.description: The wound copied the reactor wrong way up, and it put the roof on the inside. That gallery is full of stopped time, and the liquidators work it in ninety-second shifts, like the men who cleared the roof at Chernobyl by hand. At the far end stands a figure frozen in the middle of a scream, and he's Mykola Bondar, and I'm asking you to let him go. The Ninety Seconds is the long gallery up the east side of the Reactor Hall, past the Bubbler Pools, and he's at the north end, beside the breach into the core. He'll fight you, because the wound made him again and wants to keep him, so don't hesitate when you see his face, because he wouldn't want you to.
dw_let_him_go.accept_text: Tell me afterwards if he said anything. Even one word.

dw_let_it_go_out.description: My pyre hasn't gone out once since Ariden's Watch was built, because anything that died in Deadwind got up again unless it was burned. Now nothing gets up. It's time to let the fire go out. I talked to every one of them while they burned, and I'd rather not do this last part alone. Stand with me while it goes out, that's all I ask.
dw_let_it_go_out.accept_text: Stand with me, that's all. I don't want someone who'll make a speech.

dw_let_the_evening_end.description: There's a doorway in the Stopped Places that stands on its own, with no wall round it. My evening comes in through it every time it starts again. I want someone to walk through it from the other side and let the evening finish. It's north-east of here, past the elder tree. Walk through it backwards, the way the evening comes in.
dw_let_the_evening_end.accept_text: Don't turn round once you're through. Whatever's behind you can wait for morning.

dw_mograk.description: Mog'grak was Grosh'gok's chief, and he's my father. When the light came, it fused him with the boy he used to be, and the boy is the one who hurts people now. I can't fight my own father, so I'm asking you to do it for me. He's somewhere in Grosh'gok Compound. You'll know him, because there are two of him.
dw_mograk.accept_text: He's somewhere in Grosh'gok Compound. Don't listen to the small one. He was always the cruel one.

dw_nothing_up_the_sickwater.description: The Sickwater runs past the camp's well on its way south, and the Sickwater Leeches have started coming up out of it at night. I found one in the water barrel this morning. The living drink from that well, and I'd like them to keep living. Follow the Sickwater north or south of the ford, and kill every leech you see in it. I don't drink anything myself, but I've buried enough people who did.
dw_nothing_up_the_sickwater.accept_text: Check your boots when you come out of the water. They like to hide in the laces.

dw_old_three_heads.description: Old Three-Heads led the Deadwind pack for twenty years, and when the tear opened it gave him back every age he'd ever been. He hunts the Stopped Places now with a pup's head, a hunter's and an old wolf's on one body. I've watched him from the ridge, and the three heads never agree on which way to go. He keeps to the Stopped Places, round the elder tree. Go and put him down.
dw_old_three_heads.accept_text: Watch the old wolf's head most. It's the one that knows what it's doing.

dw_pages_in_the_wind.description: When Karazhan sealed, its library came apart, and the Book Flocks blew out of the windows. Every page was written by the tower's librarian, and I've noticed something strange about his hand. I've read three pages already, and I can't stop thinking about them. The Book Flocks drift round Karazhan and the Stopped Places. Catch the pages before the wind takes them over the gorge.
dw_pages_in_the_wind.accept_text: Keep them in order if you can. I've started thinking the order matters.

dw_put_them_down_kindly.description: My clan survived the tear, and that was worse than dying. They've swollen and fused together, and the ones who can still think are frightened all the time. They were my uncles and my cousins, and they used to carry me on their shoulders. They hold the ravine and the yard now. Put them down kindly, and hit them hard so it's quick.
dw_put_them_down_kindly.accept_text: If any of them says my name, tell me afterwards. I'd like to know they still had it.

dw_raise_the_spire.description: The containment spire is finished, and I want someone who helped build it standing at its foot when it lights. Kenji will be there with his dosimeters, and Morwen with her runes. If it works, the glow from the crater won't spread past it. The spire stands on the west edge of the rupture. Keep your eyes on Kenji's needle, and if it drops, we've done it.
dw_raise_the_spire.accept_text: Stand back from the base when it lights. Nobody knows quite how bright it'll be.

dw_readings_in_the_dead_forest.description: I map the fallout across the whole pass, and I need three fresh readings from the west. One from the Sickwater where it comes off the mountain, one from the Black Tarn where it pools, and one from the Widows' Wood. I'll give you a dosimeter of my own to carry, made from Seep-glass and cat gut. Hold it at arm's length and count to sixty, and don't stand in the water. At Fukushima we did this on foot for three years, house by house, until we knew every field by its number.
dw_readings_in_the_dead_forest.accept_text: Write each number down before you move. Don't trust yourself to remember three of them.

dw_samples_dead.description: I've seen what the Seep does to the living, and now I want to see what it does to the dead. The Plot Risen have marrow in them that glows. They walk Morgan's Plot and Coachman's Bend, east of here. Break the long bones and take the marrow from the break. It'll be warm, and I don't want that to alarm you.
dw_samples_dead.accept_text: Seal each sample before you take the next. I'd like to know which bone each one came from.

dw_samples_living.description: I study what the Seep does to living things, and I want glands from the Pustule Boars, whole, before they burst. The Undercity pays me to know what the Seep is, and I've got reasons of my own as well. Those reasons are my business. The boars root all through the dead forest. Cut the glands out cleanly and don't squeeze them, because I've lost two assistants to impatience.
dw_samples_living.accept_text: Pack them in the straw I gave you. A gland that bursts in your pack is a long walk home.

dw_seep_glass.description: I scavenge for the camp, and Kenji needs Seep-glass for the dosimeters he builds. The Tunnel Slagcrawlers grow it on their backs. I won't let anybody else in the camp handle the glass, so bring it straight to me. The slagcrawlers are in the cracked tunnel south of Delgado's fence. Wrap the shards before you pack them, and don't keep one for yourself, however pretty it is.
dw_seep_glass.accept_text: Hold the shards by their edges. The faces take a print, and Kenji will know whose.

dw_silk_for_the_beds.description: I want silk from the inside of the Widows' Nest, from deep in the funnel where the glow never reached. It's the only thing in the pass clean enough to sleep under. The living here don't sleep well as it is. I don't sleep myself, but I keep the beds the way I'd want one kept. The Nest is in the crag at the top of the Widows' Wood, north-east of the crossing.
dw_silk_for_the_beds.accept_text: Roll it loose, not tight. Tight silk creases, and nobody sleeps well on creases.

dw_slag_for_the_spire.description: I'm raising a containment spire at the edge of the rupture, to Kenji's design and with Morwen's runes. The base needs weight, and the heaviest thing in the pass is the slag the Gorge Slagcrawlers carry. They crawl the floor of the Sleeping Gorge. Bring me their slag and I'll pour the footings. I've built things to keep people away from places before, and this one has to hold.
dw_slag_for_the_spire.accept_text: Bring it in the iron bucket, not a sack. That slag's heavier than it looks, and hot.

dw_spiders_in_the_root_cellar.description: I keep my potatoes in a root cellar under the lean-to, and the Deadwind Widows from the wood to the north-east have started nesting in it. I went down with a lamp this morning and came back up very quickly. I'm not afraid of spiders, but these ones glow. They come from the Widows' Wood. Kill them where they breed, and they'll stop coming to me.
dw_spiders_in_the_root_cellar.accept_text: If you find my good lamp down there, bring it back up. I dropped it.

dw_still_clicking.description: Tomas's dosimeter was hanging off the handle of his cart, and it's still counting. Kenji Watanabe can read a dosimeter and tell you where a man walked and how long he stood there. I want to know where that boy went. Kenji works at his map table in Ariden's Watch, north up the old pass road. Take it to him, and scrub at the troughs before you hand it over.
dw_still_clicking.accept_text: Up the road to Deadman's Crossing, and the Watch is through the gate on your right. Scrub before you go in.

dw_tallow_for_the_pyre.description: The dead forest burns green and fast, and my pyre eats it faster than I can cut it. I've found that the tallow the Grave Oozes leave behind them burns slow and hot, and it doesn't smoke as badly. The Grave Oozes seep up out of the graves at Morgan's Plot, east of here. Skim the tallow off them and bring it back to me. This fire hasn't gone out once since the camp was built, and it isn't going to go out on my watch.
dw_tallow_for_the_pyre.accept_text: Bring it in the clay pot by the woodpile. It soaks straight through a sack.

dw_tell_halya.description: The onlookers are gone, and I can hear myself again, a little. I need you to find Halya, my sister, and tell her the readings were wrong. We measured the tear as if it were a hole, and it isn't a hole, it's something the words keep slipping off. My name's stitched inside the collar of this coat, Mykola Bondar, so she'll know it's me. Take her my notes from the bridge. Tell her I'm sorry I never came back up the rope.
dw_tell_halya.accept_text: Give her the coat as well, if she wants it. I don't think I'll be needing it.

dw_the_board_by_the_pyre.description: I keep the gate at Ariden's Watch, and every newcomer gets the same order from me. First you scrub at the troughs, and then you go and read the board by the pyre, before you do anything else. Every name on that board is someone Deadwind has taken since the camp was built. You should know who you're standing among. Read all of it, every name.
dw_the_board_by_the_pyre.accept_text: Read all of it. Old Tobiah keeps the pyre and the board, and he'll want to know you did.

dw_the_board_of_names.description: The Wound's Heart is dead, and nothing in Deadwind is getting up again. I've put my brother Mykola's name back on the board by the pyre, a little way under Tomas's. At home they read the names aloud every April, and I want it done here too. I'd like you to read them out at the pyre, all of them. Start at the top, read slowly, and don't stop until you reach Mykola.
dw_the_board_of_names.accept_text: Take your time over each one. Nobody here's in a hurry tonight.

dw_the_chained_ones.description: Grosh'gok kept beasts for war and for the pot, and the Chained Maulers were the worst of them even before the light came. Now they've fused with their own chains, and they'd tear the walls down if they could get loose. They're staked in the ravine and round the yard. Kill them where they stand. When I go for my father, I don't want anything at my back.
dw_the_chained_ones.accept_text: Mind the chains when they drop. They keep moving for a while after.

dw_the_coachmans_plate.description: My son drove the mail coach over the pass, before the plague came west. One winter he went off the road at the bend below the Plot, and the coach went over with him. The wreck still lies at Coachman's Bend, north of here on the road. The old coaches carried their driver's name on a brass plate. If it's still there, I'd know his name again.
dw_the_coachmans_plate.accept_text: Coachman's Bend is north of here, on the road. Something crashes there every few minutes, so mind the road.

dw_the_craters_edge.description: I want to salvage what's left of the first camp the liquidators built at the edge of the rupture, before they pulled back to Ariden's Watch. There's good iron in it, and some of our first tools. The Bloated Walkers wander through it, and when they burst, the seep goes everywhere. They shamble round the rupture. Kill them from a distance if you can, and stand upwind.
dw_the_craters_edge.accept_text: Bring back anything with a name scratched on it. Those tools were ours before they were salvage.

dw_the_crow_king.description: Every Many-Eyed Crow in Deadwind flies to the Drowned Hollow in the end, and I've seen why. Something there has gathered the crows into itself until it's one bird made of hundreds. The Forsaken call it the Crow King, and it sees everything every crow sees. It circles the Drowned Hollow, over the mere and the cave mouth. Take it down and the crows will scatter.
dw_the_crow_king.accept_text: Cover your eyes when it falls. The crows will all go up at once, and they won't look where they're flying.

dw_the_dogs.description: I feed a pack of strays that followed Taras's dog Kashtan out of the Watch, and the Tumour Wolves have started taking them at night. At home in Chernobyl, the dogs stayed when the people left, and the old women fed them. I'm one of those old women. The wolves circle my place at dusk. Kill them, and come back for soup.
dw_the_dogs.accept_text: Don't feed the strays on your way out. They'll follow you, and I'd rather they stayed by my door.

dw_the_drowned_thing.description: At the bottom of the Drowned Seep is the sump, where everything the drain carries ends up. Something has grown in it out of mud, roots and drowned animals. I want it dead before the Royal Apothecary Society hears about it and wants it alive. Follow the channel down through the oxbows to the sump. Kill it, and I'll write that it was already dead when you found it.
dw_the_drowned_thing.accept_text: Breathe through your mouth down there. The sump smells worse than anything you've met.

dw_the_dying_stags.description: The Dissolving Stags are coming apart while they're still walking. They come to the camp's fence at night, as if someone in here could help them. I'm a doctor, and I can't. They graze the dead forest and the shore of the Black Tarn. End it for them, please, and be quick about it.
dw_the_dying_stags.accept_text: If one comes to you on its own, let it. It might be the kindest way.

dw_the_elephants_foot.description: At the bottom of the Exclusion Zone, under the reactor the wound copied, is the knot that keeps every copy it makes: flesh, black glass and stopped light, fused into one mass. I gave it its name the first time I saw it. Under Chernobyl's reactor the core melted through the floor and set in the basement as fuel, sand and concrete, and they called it the Elephant's Foot, and five minutes beside it would kill you. Go in through the breach to the Lid and take the stair down beside it, and the Steam Corridor goes three sides round the basement before it lets you in. The Wound's Heart is on an island in the melt, and killing it won't close the tear, but it'll stop it remembering, and then what dies in Deadwind can stay dead.
dw_the_elephants_foot.accept_text: Don't look at it longer than you need to. I did, the first time, and I still see it.

dw_the_four_chains.description: The wheel's gondolas hang on chains over the glow crater, and Morwen's runes have to be cut into the chains themselves for the spire to hold. I've got the runes pressed into wax tablets. I need someone to stand under the wheel on both sides and press them on. The wheel is in the rupture, east of the Stopped Places. Hold each tablet flat for a slow count of ten, and don't look up at the gondolas.
dw_the_four_chains.accept_text: If the chains swing, wait for them to settle. The runes won't take if the wax slips.

dw_the_glow_eater.description: The Exclusion Zone doesn't stop under the wheel. Below the first floor the wound has built a copy of the reactor, and its flooded basement holds two pools of the seep that the liquidators call the Bubbler Pools. Something lives between them that eats the seep and grows on it, and I call it the Glow-Eater. Kenji's readings say it's the reason the pulses from the wheel have been getting stronger. Take the stair down the shaft at the wheel's hub into the Reactor Hall, then follow the turbine hall south to the flooded basement, and don't give it time to feed.
dw_the_glow_eater.accept_text: Keep out of the pools themselves. Whatever's in that water is what it's been eating.

dw_the_last_egg.description: The Silk Mother is a widow queen who has grown into her own cocoon at the bottom of the Widows' Nest, and her eggs glow. I want the last of them alive, taken from the brood chamber itself. If the Seep can grow a brood like that, it can grow a hand back. Halyna and Dr. Seitkali want the whole brood burned, and only one of us can have it. The brood is at the top of the Throat, past the retreat holes.
dw_the_last_egg.accept_text: The brood's at the top of the Throat. Kill the Silk Mother and bring me the egg she's sitting on, warm.

dw_the_master_isnt_dining.description: Karazhan's servants wandered out before the tower sealed, and they're still serving a dinner nobody came to. The Spectral Servants carry cold trays across the Vice, and the Ballroom Phantoms dance with anyone they catch. They took my wife's dance the year the tower went dark. They gather at Karazhan's foot, round the old stables. Let them rest, because dinner's been over for a very long time.
dw_the_master_isnt_dining.accept_text: If one of them asks you to dance, say yes. It's quicker than saying no.

dw_the_ogre_at_the_ravine.description: An ogre came to the gate three nights ago, alone and unarmed, and asked for help in a child's voice. I sent him away with a bone token and a promise that someone would come. I keep my promises, even to ogres. His name is Grull, and he's waiting on the ravine road outside Grosh'gok Compound. Go west from Deadman's Crossing, up Deadwind Ravine, and show him the token.
dw_the_ogre_at_the_ravine.accept_text: Hold the token where he can see it before you get close. He frightens easily.

dw_the_ones_that_got_up.description: The dead at Morgan's Plot don't stay in the ground any more, and I can't carry them all back to my pyre by myself. They were buried once, properly, by people who loved them. Something dug them up and wore them, and that isn't their fault. The Plot Risen walk the graves south of Coachman's Bend, under the cliff. Put them back down, and I'll go out with the cart tonight and bring them home.
dw_the_ones_that_got_up.accept_text: Leave them face up if you can. I'd like them to see the sky on the way home.

dw_the_onlookers.description: I'm stuck on the broken bridge over the Sleeping Gorge, in the middle of a stride, and I only get a few words out each time the moment comes round. The Bridge Onlookers crowd round me, and every time one of them touches me I lose a word. They came to watch the glow the night the tear opened, and they stayed. There are too many of them, and they won't stop watching. Get them away from me, because I'm trying to remember something.
dw_the_onlookers.accept_text: Please hurry, because I've nearly got it back.

dw_the_readings_were_wrong.description: The readings were wrong. I keep saying it, and now I can see why I keep saying it. Down there, south-east, the river stopped on the floor of the Sleeping Gorge. Stand in the water that doesn't move, and look which way it's leaning. Then come back and tell me, before I lose the words again.
dw_the_readings_were_wrong.accept_text: Look carefully, and come back quickly. I don't get many words.

dw_the_runners_cart.description: A crack opened in the mountain on the far side of the Rotvine Fen when the worlds came together. The liquidators up in Deadwind Pass, newcomers every one of them, send a runner down through it for supplies. Their runner, Tomas, has come through Grom'gol every week for a year, and I've come to like the boy. This week he left with a handcart of iodine and bandages, and nobody at the far end has seen him. The tunnel's in the rock past the fen, east of the Steps, so follow the cart ruts and find out what happened.
dw_the_runners_cart.accept_text: If you find the cart, check whether the iodine's still in it. That tells us a lot.

dw_the_totem_in_the_bones.description: Our clan totem had the handprint of every ogre born in the compound painted on it. When the light came, the Sore-Shamans broke it apart for their fires. My own handprint is on it, from when I was very small. I want the pieces back. The Sore-Shamans carry them in their bags, in the yard past the gate.
dw_the_totem_in_the_bones.accept_text: Look for a very small handprint. That one's mine.

dw_the_volunteers_kits.description: Liquidators went down into the Exclusion Zone before the camp knew what was down there, and some of them are still there, stopped or aged to dust where they stood. I want their kits back. Every kit has a name stitched inside the flap. The Stopped Volunteers and the Aged Volunteers are in the Reactor Hall and all the way down the Steam Corridor. Bring me every kit you find, masks and all, because the families can't have the bodies, but they can have these.
dw_the_volunteers_kits.accept_text: Read the names to yourself as you pick them up. I'd like somebody to have said them down there.

dw_the_well.description: I drink from the old well on the shore of the Black Tarn, and lately the water tastes of pennies. I've drunk from it every morning since I came here, and it never tasted of anything before. The well's south-east of here, on the tarn's north-east shore, with the stone ring round it. Go and look down it, and tell me what you see. Kenji will tell me not to drink from it, and I'll ignore him.
dw_the_well.accept_text: Don't lean too far over. The stones on the ring are loose.

dw_this_evening.description: I've watched Karazhan from my camp on the rim of the Sleeping Gorge for forty years. Every evening the light in the tower's high window goes out at exactly the same moment. Since the tear, I think I've been living the same evening over and over, and I only half know it. I'd like you to go to the tower's foot and look up at that window. I can never tell from here whether the light's going out or coming on.
dw_this_evening.accept_text: Down the gorge and east through the Vice, to the tower's gate. Look up at the high window.

dw_three_ages_of_a_wolf.description: The Three-Age Wolves of the Ashen Rise have three heads, and I'm sure they're the same wolf at three ages. A pup, a grown hunter and an old grey, and all three heads are hungry. They hunt the open ground and the slopes under the Hanging Slide. Thin them out for me. Go for the old head first, because it's the one that remembers how to fight.
dw_three_ages_of_a_wolf.accept_text: Go when they're hunting, not resting. The pup's head gets careless when it's hungry.

dw_too_many_eyes.description: The Many-Eyed Crows sit along the fence posts and watch the camp, and I swear they watch in shifts. The Forsaken say crows like that carry what they see back to whatever made them. I don't care what they're carrying, I care that they're watching. They're all over the dead forest. Shoot the ones on the fence first.
dw_too_many_eyes.accept_text: If one flies off toward the east, follow it with your eyes. I want to know where they report.

dw_what_a_liquidator_is.description: I run Ariden's Watch, and I've got work for anyone Tobiah sends to me. The Tumour Wolves come down out of the dead forest after our supply carts, and they've taken two drivers this month. Without the carts, this camp starves in a fortnight. I want the road kept clear between the fence and Deadman's Crossing. Don't let them bite you, and wash at the troughs every time you come back.
dw_what_a_liquidator_is.accept_text: The Tumour Wolves hunt along the pass road. Don't get bitten, and wash at the troughs when you come back.

dw_what_comes_up.description: Every time the spire grows, the rupture answers it. The Fused Masses heave themselves up out of the crater, and the Many-Armed Things reach for the scaffolding. My crew can't work with them at their backs. They come up all round the rupture, so keep them off the spire. Kill the Many-Armed Things first, because they're the ones that pull my crew off the ladders.
dw_what_comes_up.accept_text: Stay off the ladders yourself. They weren't built for fighting on.

dw_what_master_ashgrave_keeps.description: I'm Morwen Ashgrave's second, and I'm worried about her. She locks her own notes in the sealed store behind the laboratory, and lately she's been taking samples in there and not bringing them out. I can't be seen going in myself, because she'd know at once. The store is behind the laboratory, south-east of here. The lock is made for the living, so you'll get past it, and I only need you to look.
dw_what_master_ashgrave_keeps.accept_text: Leave everything exactly where it is. She'll notice a jar out of place.

dw_what_the_wolves_carry.description: I run the infirmary here, and I want to understand these tumours before they turn up in my patients. The Tumour Wolves carry them in every stage, from the first swelling to the last. I've seen growths like these before, at home, and I need to know if they behave the same. The wolves run the dead forest along the pass road. Cut the growths out and wrap each one separately, because I'll want to know how fast they grow.
dw_what_the_wolves_carry.accept_text: Label each one with the date. The speed is what I'm after.

dw_whats_in_the_water.description: The fallout pools in the Drowned Hollow and drains down through the hill into a cave the Forsaken call the Drowned Seep. I've got a theory about it. Every time the leeches in the Seep breed, the camp's well goes bad a week later. The Seep is in the hill above the mere, in the south-west of Deadwind East. Clear the leeches and we'll see if I'm right.
dw_whats_in_the_water.accept_text: Don't drink from the well for a week after. I'll know by then whether I was right.
